newsitem.title: CHINA: China stages electronic warfare exercises.
newsitem.headline: China stages electronic warfare exercises.

text.p: China said on Sunday it had recently staged long-distance military exercises combining air and ground manoeuvres with electronic warfare.
The live-fire war games were designed to test the ability to move men and equipment over long distances and to coordinate different fighting units, the Liberation Army Daily said.
Aircraft, missiles, artillery, armoured vehicles and ground troops were used in the war games that also tested electronic jamming and countermeasures, the army newspaper said.
"The success of the exercises demonstrated that we have taken a major step forward in our long-distance fighting capabilities, using mechanised and coordinated battle skills," it said.
The exercises were organised by People's Liberation Army units of the Jinan military district, headquartered in the eastern province of Shandong.
The newspaper did not say how many troops took part or when or where the war games were held.

But it said that mock air and ground attacks were staged in the Tongbai mountains of Henan and Hubei provinces in central China and along the Taihang mountains which straddle the border between the northern provinces of Hebei and Shanxi.

China has been trying to modernise its three-million-strong armed forces, adopting more sophisticated equipment and abandoning the old strategies of "people's warfare" that once relied on guerrilla tactics.

Senior Chinese leaders, including President and Communist Party chief Jiang Zemin, have pushed hard to enhance the electronic warfare capabilities of the armed forces. Jiang is also chairman of the Communist Party's powerful Central Military Commission.
